SM23L-A1.free_elimination: None free. Option set holds two (x,y) pairs on x+2y=-26: (-10,-8) and (30,-28), so the x-coordinates are visible as distractors but nothing is struck without solving. Plug-back ascending hits -28 first and it PASSES both equations (k=5) - rejecting it needs the uniqueness decision (det=0 at k=5).
SM23L-A1.note: y(k-9)=112 and y(5-2k)=10+26k give 26k^2=650, k=+-5; k=5 makes the system dependent/parallel (det k(k-1)-20=0), so k=-5, x=-10, y=-8. Off-blueprint flag is borderline: the item is a 2x2 parametric system plus a THIRD linear condition, and the solve is quadratic in k; the brief lists a third equation as off-blueprint.

SM23L-A2.note: x=2y-3; y(2k+4)=5+3k and y(k+17)=28 give 3k^2=27, k=+-3; k=3 gives det 3*8-24=0 (not exactly one point), so k=-3, y=28/14=2, x=1. Same borderline third-equation blueprint flag as A1; structurally A1 and A2 are the same template.

SM23L-A5.free_elimination: None strictly free. Range width 16 over width 4 gives |a|=4, so f(8) is 9+20=29 or -7-20=-27 - that is most of the work, not a free strike. f(8) is not checkable by substitution.
SM23L-A5.note: Increasing case a=4, b=-3 (negative intercept, rejected); decreasing a=-4, b=5 -> f(8)=-27. The decision (which endpoint maps to which) is a two-case check any careful student does routinely.

SM23L-A6.free_elimination: None free. All four are 8*(k-range width) for different endpoint pairings; nothing strikes without the work. Plug-back n/a (difference of extremes).
SM23L-A6.note: f(x)=k(x-1)+4 pivots on (1,4); constraints at x=-2 and x=5: -2<=k<=4/3 and -1<=k<=3/2 -> k in [-1,4/3]; f(9)=4+8k spans 8*(7/3)=56/3. Decision: intersecting both endpoint constraints (each distractor keeps a wrong bound). A slider can approximate but 4/3 is hard to read off.

SM23L-A7.free_elimination: Direction: a solution set 'x <= ...' requires the x-coefficient k-4 to be negative, so k<4, striking 9 (this IS the item's intended decision). Then 25/(k-4)=k-4 needs (k-4)^2=25: options give k-4 = -13, -9, -5, so -9 and -5 die on sight. Plug-back ascending reaches the key in 3 tries, each a one-line check.
SM23L-A7.note: (k-4)x>=25; for <= need k-4<0, x<=25/(k-4)=k-4 -> (k-4)^2=25 -> k-4=-5 -> k=-1. Only one non-key option is ever a candidate (9, the no-flip root).

SM23L-B7.free_elimination: None free. Count asked; plug-back n/a. 46 sits beside 51 (all of 1..51) and 15/17 (integer-k readings); no free strike.

Possible ambiguity worth noting: a student could read 'values of k' as integer k, but the stem does not say integer, so 46 is the defensible key.
